title: Publicis Wins PepsiCo's $5.4 Billion Media Account, Exits Coca-Cola Pitch
excerpt: The French agency group displaces Omnicom as PepsiCo's lead global media partner in a deal covering 200-plus markets, and withdraws from rival Coca-Cola's ongoing review.
body:
• PepsiCo appointed Publicis Groupe as its exclusive lead global media partner, displacing Omnicom's OMD network after more than 20 years
  • The "One PepsiCo" model will cover media strategy, planning, and activation across 200-plus markets for brands including Pepsi, Gatorade, and Lay's
  • Publicis will withdraw from Coca-Cola's ongoing $4 billion global media review due to the conflict of interest
  • There was no formal pitch — PepsiCo selected Publicis after a media capabilities review focused on AI and data integration

PepsiCo has named Publicis Groupe as its exclusive lead global media partner, handing the French advertising group one of the biggest account wins in the industry's recent history. The appointment displaces Omnicom's OMD network, which had held PepsiCo's media business in key markets including the United States and United Kingdom for more than two decades.

The deal, confirmed by PepsiCo to ADWEEK, will see Publicis build a new "One PepsiCo" media operating model that unites strategy, planning, activation, connected identity, and technology under one roof across more than 200 markets. PepsiCo spent $5.4 billion on marketing activities in 2025, with $3.4 billion going toward advertising, according to its latest annual report.

No Pitch, Just Capabilities

In a departure from the typical agency selection process, there was no formal pitch. PepsiCo conducted a media capabilities review and selected Publicis on the strength of its AI and data-driven marketing infrastructure. The decision signals a broader shift in how major advertisers evaluate agency partners — prioritizing technology platforms over creative presentations.

https://x.com/Campaignmag/status/2095233564254015743

"Powered by data and AI, this transformation will help PepsiCo deliver more relevant consumer connections, make smarter marketing decisions across paid, earned, shared and owned to improve the impact of its media investments."

— PepsiCo spokesperson

Publicis had previously worked with PepsiCo in markets including China, India, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, South Korea, Indonesia, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and parts of Eastern Europe. The global consolidation extends that relationship to every market in PepsiCo's portfolio.

Coca-Cola Pitch Abandoned

The PepsiCo win creates an immediate conflict of interest. According to sources cited by ADWEEK and Campaign, Publicis will withdraw from the ongoing pitch for the remainder of Coca-Cola's global media business, a review estimated to be worth approximately $4 billion. MediaSense is handling that review, which began in July.

Publicis had been in a shootout against WPP for the Coca-Cola account. The French group already handles Coca-Cola's media in the U.S. and Canada, a contract it won from WPP last year. Coca-Cola's review covers all top markets globally, excluding North America and Japan/Korea where it works with Dentsu.

WPP, the incumbent through its bespoke Open X unit, now appears positioned to retain or expand its Coca-Cola relationship by default. Coca-Cola reported $5.4 billion in advertising expenses in 2025, with $2.6 billion spent on media globally.

Impact on Omnicom

For Omnicom, losing PepsiCo's media mandate after more than 20 years is a significant blow. PepsiCo said Omnicom will remain a "critical strategic partner" across creative, sports marketing, and public relations, but the media account — the largest revenue line — moves entirely to Publicis. Bank of America analysts estimated the PepsiCo win could boost Publicis's 2027 organic net revenue growth by 50 to 100 basis points.

What's Next

PepsiCo is separately conducting a global review of AI marketing transformation capabilities, with Omnicom, Accenture, Deloitte, and Publicis's Sapient unit competing for that brief. The dual reviews underscore how AI integration is reshaping the advertising industry's competitive landscape at the holding-company level.
